pr_title: Don't try to create VolumeSpec immediately after underlying PVC is being deleted
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
As @mm4tt mentioned in #86434, when PVC is being deleted, desired_state_of_world_populator shouldn't try to create VolumeSpec.

This PR is a performance bug fix.

The fix is rebased on @jingxu97 's comment:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86670#issuecomment-569823371

Original proposal is to add map pvcsUnderDeletion to desiredStateOfWorldPopulator.
The map is from namespaced claim name to the earliest time when next GET request to api-server is made.
The proposal is able to handle generic api server error return and limits the change within desired_state_of_world_populator.go

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #86434

```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```docs

```
pr_comments: /test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce
/cc @msau42

I renamed the map pvcsUnderDeletion (using plural) to distinguish from the constant.

For test coverage, after running through desired_state_of_world_populator_test.go, I haven't found how the following would be hit:
```
		if pvc.ObjectMeta.DeletionTimestamp != nil {
			return nil, errors.New(pvcBeingDeleted)
```
I think the best proof is the (significantly) reduced QPS in load test (ref #86434).

For #2, findAndRemoveDeletedPods is the only func which handles pod removal from volume.
Cleansing pvcsUnderDeletion is covered.
/priority important-soon

I tried to add the following call in test to mimic PVC under deletion:
```
	var err error
	err = dswp.kubeClient.CoreV1().PersistentVolumeClaims(namespace).Delete(pvcName, &metav1.DeleteOptions{})
```
However, desiredStateOfWorldPopulator#processPodVolumes has the following check at the beginning:
```
	if dswp.podPreviouslyProcessed(uniquePodName) {
		return false
```
So the second call to desiredStateOfWorldPopulator#processPodVolumes would short-circuit.
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-storage-slow
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce

Examining kubelet log from e2e-gce test, I saw the following (where skipping call to dswp.createVolumeSpec was added) - showing the effectiveness of the change:
```
I1229 04:01:55.338602  187327 desired_state_of_world_populator.go:334] pvc pv-1572/pvc-4jch6 is being deleted, pod pvc-tester-l5v7k, volume volume1
```
Let me think about mocking - though our goal is to test desiredStateOfWorldPopulator, not its mock.

Thanks @tedyu for tackling this!

I'm leaving the review to the sig-node, but looking at the `pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce-100-performance` test the fix seems to be helping. The number of GET PVC requests went down from ~3300 to ~700 in a 100 node cluster.
Thanks @tedyu ! I'll try and find time to look at these updates either tomorrow or Wednesday.
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce

/assign @jingxu97 @saad-ali 
@kubernetes/sig-storage-pr-reviews

Thank you for tackling this issue. 

My 2 cents: creating a cache of PVs that are being deleted is a pretty hacky fix -- it may result in cache skew issues. I think the right fix would be to use an informer instead of direct gets. But, kubelet can't do that due a a number of issues (node authorizer, race between PV deltion and pod scheduling, etc.). @msau42 spoke about this offline and she has good suggestion that she'll add to this thread.

CC @cduchesne for FYI -- he's looked in to PV/PVC scalability issues as well.

@saad-ali and I discussed this a bit, and have some concerns with the overall approach. This is a very targeted fix that adds a cache for this very specific error. It's one more cache that can get out of sync and has the potential to leak if we don't clean it up in all the right places.

I think a better approach would be to restructure the dsw populator to use exponential backoff per pod. Right now the retry period is very frequent (100ms), and I think the other populator error conditions would benefit from having a backoff as well.
I took a look at pkg/kubelet/pluginmanager/operationexecutor/operation_executor.go which does not seem to be involved with populator.

I think the exponential backoff is a variant of my first proposal where the map is used to indicate the earliest time (or set of parameters which facilitate the calculation of such time) when the next Get request is to be made if most recent Get encounters error.
If the PVC is available, there is no entry in the map.

We can clear the entry in map inside the dswp.desiredStateOfWorld.GetPodsWithErrors() loop:
```
	podsWithError := dswp.desiredStateOfWorld.GetPodsWithErrors()
	for _, podName := range podsWithError {
```
I am still studying related code. The benefit of above variant is that coupling between modules (pluginmanager and volumemanager) is under control.

We should choose the interval between successive Gets for the same PVC in case of (general) error.
If the interval is too long, we lose responsiveness for the VolumeSpec to be created in a timely manner.

I think we can add a workqueue of 1 concurrency keyed on pod name between `findAndAddNewPods()` and `processPodVolumes`. The workqueue interface is nice because it handles the exponential backoff, along with caching of the key + timestamp. In the future, we could even consider increasing the concurrency if we want to.  The main tricky bit is that we have to make sure to remove the Pod from the workqueue when the Pod is terminated or deleted.
/cc @jingxu97

the workflow related to this issue is as follows

1. After pod is first scheduled to the node, desired_state_populator adds the volume/pod into the desired state and mark the pod as processed in the cache.
2. kubelet has syncPod() which periodically (occurred every 10 seconds): inside this function, it will trigger volume manager to reprocess pod by marking pod as not processed (remove pod from processedPod list)
3. Once pod is not in processedPod list, desired_state_populator will loop the pod (in every 100 ms) and get the PVC/PV information from API server to update the desired state. The problem comes from here. If PVC/PV is failed to retrieve from API server, desired_state_populator will keep looping the pod and issue get calls every 100 ms until it gets it and mark pod as processed.
So in the test, when PVC/PV is deleted before pod, this behavior will happen.

Discussed with @saad-ali @msau42, initially we were thinking this reprocess volume mount behavior should only apply to inline ephemeral volumes such as secrets. However, it won't work because two reasons. First, volume resize feature also relies on pod reprocess feature so that it can get updated pvc objects to check whether the requested size is changed. Second, reprocess is applied to pod, not volume. A pod might have different types of volumes.

Now we are thinking another way to solve it. Look at the logic here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L357, it means that only if all volumes of a pod have been added to desired state without error, the pod is marked as processed so that desired_state_populator will not continue to loop for this pod's volumes. There are two possible ways to fix issue around this code.
1. Remove the check on [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L357), it means that even if some or all volumes of this pod could not be added at the moment, we still mark pod as processed. Although desired_state_populator will not continue to loop on this pod for a moment, after kubelet's syncPod is called, the pod will be removed from processedPod list and then it will be reprocessed. The behavior will changed in different conditions as follows
1) When the pod is processed in desired state populator, if it fails to get pvc/pv objects due to temporal API server issue, it needs to wait about 10 seconds to get a chance to be processed again.
2) If the pvc/pv referenced by pod no longer exists, desired_state_populator will not constantly process the pod's volumes by calling API servers. Instead, it will wait until next syncPod happens to reprocess the volumes.

The second behavior is desired for fixing the issue. However the first changed behavior might slow down pod starts up in the case of temporal API server issue or network issue, although it should be very rare. One way to overcome this is we still keep the check in this [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L357), however we could add the logic to check if pod and volumes have been processed before (volumes were added into the desired state already), then even if it cannot retrieve the new pvc/pv in this round, we can still mark pod as processed and wait until next round to get the most updated pvc/pv. We can get this information by checking whether a pod's volume has been already added into the desired state before. If it is true, remove the check in [line](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L357), otherwise, keep it.

When the dswp.desiredStateOfWorld.AddPodToVolume() call is made conditional in processPodVolumes(), as shown here:
```
		if present, err := dswp.desiredStateOfWorld.IsVolumeSeenByDSW(uniquePodName, volumeSpec); err == nil && present {
			volumePreviouslyAdded = true
		} else {
			// Add volume to desired state of world
			_, err = dswp.desiredStateOfWorld.AddPodToVolume(
				uniquePodName, pod, volumeSpec, podVolume.Name, volumeGidValue)
```

```
[sig-storage] Projected downwardAPI should update labels on modification [NodeConformance] [Conformance] expand_more    2m7s
[sig-storage] Downward API volume should update annotations on modification [NodeConformance] [Conformance] 
```

I wonder @jingxu97 's suggestion on using previously added volume to judge whether pod is processed or not covers all the error cases around PersistentVolumeClaim.

For PersistentVolumeClaim under deletion, this probably will work. But in some situation, e.g. if api-server times out leading to uncertainty in volumemanager on whether the underlying PersistentVolumeClaim is created, there wouldn't be volume added to dsw. This way, the number of requests to api-server would not come down.

For modified version of my proposal where the value of map indicates the earliest time for next query to api-server, it can handle general error by not matching pvcBeingDeletedMsg text.

@tedyu , I think the logic you mentioned here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86670#issuecomment-569864310 seems right to me. But the logic you implemented here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/86670#issuecomment-569952054 seems different from the above? It will skip AddPodToVolume if volume has been processed before?
@tedyu, yes that 's what I meant. I forgot to put the link there. So for the current PR, do you still have test failures?
For the current PR, tests pass.
I feel the current PR is small change and fix the issue we have for now. We can work on it further to solve issues you mentioned after this PR. What do you think?

@jingxu97 
Good by me.
@tedyu do you mind to explain your original proposal as comments or somewhere? Want to think a little more on how to better handle this all together. Thanks!

@jingxu97 
Please let me know which approach to pursue (keeping a map of next GET request time versus the current formation).

@tedyu, sorry for the delay. I checked the proposal, it solves the issue in a different way. I think it handles the situation of pvc is being deleted (pvc still exist, but has deletiontimestamp set), how about other situation like pvc is already deleted?
In your previous comment, "a map of next GET request time", do you mean your original proposal "map pvcsUnderDeletion to desiredStateOfWorldPopulator". 

Like I mentioned, I am ok with this change for now. We can work further later for solving better the generic problem. Just want to have a second reviewer to agree on this.
 cc @saad-ali @msau42

w.r.t. 'situation like pvc is already deleted', we only check the err, not error text. So it should be covered.

w.r.t. 'a map of next GET request time', suppose at T1 the GET request for pvc fails, T1+delay (100 seconds e.g.) would be stored in the map so that the next GET request isn't sent before that.

I agree that the current approach achieves reduction in load on api-server.
We can go with current formation.

i don't see other concerns from other reviewers. 
So /lgtm

@jingxu97 
Can you put the /lgtm on its own line ?

Considering @msau42 and @gnufied 's comments, shall we switch back to my proposal of tracking the next GET request time in case of api server error ?
I think the GET approach is very specific to these two checks. I would prefer a solution that is more generic and can handle other errors as well.

The other option is to use https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/util/manager/cache_based_manager.go which is already being used for caching secrets and configmaps in kubelet , but that probably requires larger refactor(and testing).

issue_context.title: Kubelets issue 2K QPS of GET PersistentVolumeClaim requests during 5K node load test
issue_context.body:
It happens during the "delete" phase in the load test.

![Vc5Ms0vcuCo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2604887/71180511-a0589f00-2272-11ea-858d-8015a6a9ab8d.png)

In perf-dash we can see that in total there are ~20M requests like that during the load test.

![4WrEtLhXEh9](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2604887/71180626-e01f8680-2272-11ea-9204-aff990067727.png)

It started in Sep 2019 (sic!), so probably when we enabled PVs in our load tests. We haven't detected it so far as, strangely, it doesn't seem to be impacting our scalability SLIs.

We should investigate this.

/sig scalability
comments: I checked and we create 35 PersistentVolumeClaims per 100 nodes. So in case of 5K node test there will be 1750 PVCs in the cluster. This is close to the 2K of GET PVC requests we see.

Let's analyze the last run of 5K node test in more depths  - https://prow.k8s.io/view/gcs/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-scale-performance/1210244261132374016

![WD7UnSp9PSy](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2604887/71519620-a674fe00-28b8-11ea-9aab-35cdb023a2e8.png)

As I wrote already somewhere here, it happens during the delete phase. We reach the peak of ~2K QPS around 2:30 AM UTC in that run. Let's check the logs (api-server, kubelets) around that time.
